comment: CT-3 — verifies that a server (or client) MUST reject a snapshot whose chunk content has been mutated, even when a local Merkle branch is recomputed to be self-consistent against the mutated chunk. Spec authority: cokret-spec/spec/v1/zh/conformance/snapshot-schema.md §3 (chunk descriptor.sha256 covers chunk payload canonical JSON bytes), §4 (state_digest MUST be the canonical Merkle root over reducer output leaves), §5 (signature covers manifest payload), §6 (event_set_commitment.root + merkle_branch inclusion proofs). The signed manifest pins state_digest, event_set_commitment.root and each chunk.sha256 — recomputing a local Merkle branch from a mutated chunk does not recover the signed root, so the snapshot MUST be rejected. Spec note: snapshot-schema.md does not currently use the field name 'audit_path'; the normative inclusion-proof field is `merkle_branch` (§6). The errcode is `digest_mismatch` per error-code-registry.json (canonical entry for content/digest verification failure).

vectors.name: byte_flip_in_chunk_audit_path_recomputed_still_rejected
vectors.description: Take a valid snapshot, flip one byte in chunks[0] payload bytes, then recompute the local merkle_branch for the mutated chunk so the local-recompute Merkle is internally consistent. The resulting recomputed event_set_commitment.root differs from the snapshot manifest's signed root — so verification MUST fail with digest_mismatch. The signed manifest pins the root; local recompute cannot rebind it.

expected.rationale: Even though the prover recomputed a self-consistent local Merkle, the signed manifest's chunk.sha256 and event_set_commitment.root are pinned by the snapshot signature (§5). Local recompute mismatching the signed root is the canonical digest_mismatch case.

vectors.name: byte_flip_in_audit_path_only
vectors.description: Leave the chunk payload intact (chunk.sha256 unchanged) but flip one byte inside one element of the merkle_branch (inclusion-proof path) presented to the verifier. The branch no longer hashes up to the signed event_set_commitment.root, so the verifier MUST reject. Per snapshot-schema.md §6 rule 2, every merkle_branch MUST verify against commitment_root; a tampered branch fails this check.

expected.rationale: §6 rule 2: merkle_branch MUST verify against commitment_root. A byte flip in the branch alone breaks this; chunk content can still be canonical, but the proof is unusable.

vectors.name: chunk_count_mismatch
vectors.description: Drop the last chunk from the snapshot's chunks[] array but keep the manifest's declared chunk count (e.g. event_set_commitment.covered_event_count or implied length from the signed manifest). The snapshot MUST be rejected. Per §4 (state_digest leaves are 1-to-1 with chunks[i].items[].object) and §5 (signature covers manifest payload), dropping a chunk falsifies state_digest recomputation and breaks the signed manifest's chunk coverage commitment.

expected.rationale: Dropping a chunk reduces the leaf set used to recompute state_digest; the recomputed root cannot equal the signed state_digest. Even if the manifest tried to elide the count, the event_set_commitment.root would also fail recomputation.
